facts.fact: Decree 2024-073 of 15 May 2024 states that any poor household enrolled in the Registre Social is eligible for Tekavoul regular transfers (Art. 11) and any vulnerable household enrolled in it for shock-response transfers (Art. 13), so the Registre Social is in use to choose recipients.

note: No fact for programmes or national ID link: Tekavoul and its shock component are one programme, and the decree names no ID link.

facts.fact: The World Bank blog says Mauritania is implementing a universal social registry covering the entire population.

AMI reports the economy minister told the National Assembly the IDA-financed social safety-net operation funds technical assistance to assess the continuous-update method and review the procedures of Mauritania's social registry.

Le Quotidien de Nouakchott reports that a World Bank IDA financing signed 21 August 2026 is to strengthen Mauritania's Registre social, described as the tool that identifies vulnerable households to target public interventions.
